title: Brooks' theorem for subcubic graphs
abstract: Proves that every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most three with no four-clique admits a three-colouring, without a connectedness assumption. Includes controlled greedy colouring, colouring across cut vertices, and a good-triple argument for cubic components. This is the subcubic case of Brooks' theorem, not the general-degree theorem.

informal.BrooksSubcubic.brooks_cubic: Every finite simple graph with maximum degree at most three and no clique on four vertices is three-colourable. The graph may be disconnected.
